summary: Guyana lets CARICOM nationals live and travel freely under Caribbean Community arrangements and admits a broad list of Commonwealth, European and American passports visa-free for up to 90 days; everyone else needs a visa arranged in advance through a Guyanese mission.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on the day you arrive. CARICOM nationals traveling on a national ID card under free-movement arrangements should still carry a passport for onward connections.

Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Guyana

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers aged 1 year and over arriving from, or having transited more than 12 hours in, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission. Guyana is itself a yellow fever risk country, so vaccination is strongly recommended for all visitors — and neighboring countries will ask for the certificate when you travel on.

vaccinations.name: Malaria prophylaxis
vaccinations.text: Not an entry requirement, but malaria is present in the interior regions — especially Regions 1, 7, 8 and 9 and the mining districts. Discuss prophylaxis with a travel clinic if you are going beyond the coastal belt.

travelInsurance.text: Insurance is not checked at the border, but medical facilities outside Georgetown are very limited and serious cases are evacuated to Trinidad, Barbados or the United States — cover that includes medical evacuation is strongly recommended.

source.name: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Guyana

onwardTicket.text: Immigration officers and airlines routinely ask visa-free visitors for a confirmed return or onward ticket and an address in Guyana; the permitted stay is written into your passport on arrival and is often shorter than the maximum.

source.name: Ministry of Home Affairs of Guyana

proofOfFunds.text: No fixed sum is published, but officers may ask how you will support yourself and where you are staying — carry your hotel booking and a card or some cash.

source.name: Ministry of Home Affairs of Guyana

declarations.name: Immigration arrival and departure card
declarations.text: A paper immigration card is handed out on the flight or at Cheddi Jagan International Airport and must be completed before the immigration desk. Keep the departure half in your passport — you will be asked for it when you leave.

source.name: Ministry of Home Affairs of Guyana

currencyLimits.text: Cash and negotiable instruments worth more than the equivalent of about USD 10,000 must be declared to customs on arrival and departure — confirm the current threshold with the Guyana Revenue Authority, as it is set in Guyanese dollars.

notes: Firearms, ammunition and camouflage-pattern clothing are restricted — leave them at home.
Gold and raw diamonds cannot simply be carried out: exporting them requires a license from the Guyana Gold Board or the Geology and Mines Commission.
Fresh produce, plants and untreated wildlife products are controlled — declare anything of the sort rather than risk a fine.

payments.text: Cards work in Georgetown's larger hotels, supermarkets and the oil-sector business district, but almost nowhere else — and foreign cards are frequently declined. Bring US dollars in cash to change at a licensed cambio, and carry small Guyanese notes for taxis, minibuses and the interior, where there are no ATMs at all.

safety.text: Guyana has a high rate of violent and armed crime, concentrated in Georgetown — particularly Stabroek Market, Tiger Bay and the seawall after dark. Use pre-booked taxis rather than minibuses at night, keep phones and jewellery out of sight, and treat interior travel as remote wilderness travel with no quick rescue.

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Guyana Travel Advisory

bestTimeToVisit.text: Guyana has two dry seasons — mid-February to April and mid-August to November. The later one gives the best flying weather for Kaieteur Falls and the driest tracks in the Rupununi savannah; the long May–July rains flood the interior.

idp.text: Guyana is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here.

driving.text: Guyana is a party to the 1968 Vienna Convention on Road Traffic but not to the 1949 Geneva one, so the International Driving Permit it is bound to recognize is the 1968 Vienna version. A permit issued under the 1949 Geneva Convention carries no treaty obligation here. Whether a permit is required in addition to a national license, and for how long a foreign license may be used, are set by national road law and have not been checked for Guyana yet.

tips.text: Guyana drives on the left, roads outside the coastal strip are unpaved, and night driving is genuinely dangerous — unlit vehicles, livestock and deep potholes. Hire a driver rather than self-driving if you are heading inland.

This is a cash economy. Change US dollars at a licensed cambio (never on the street), take enough Guyanese dollars for the whole interior leg before you fly out of Ogle, and expect to be quoted large numbers — G$1,000 is only a few US dollars.

Kaieteur Falls, the Rupununi and most eco-lodges are reached by small aircraft from Eugene F. Correia (Ogle) airport, not the main international airport. Baggage allowances are strict — often around 20 lb (9 kg) — and flights are weather-dependent, so leave a buffer day before an international connection.

Even visa-free visitors are given a specific number of days by the officer at the desk — often 30 rather than the full allowance. Check the stamp before you leave the counter and apply to the Central Immigration and Passport Office in Georgetown if you need longer; overstaying brings fines and delays at departure.

Carry your yellow fever certificate with your passport. It is checked if you arrive from a risk country, and Brazil, Suriname and several onward destinations ask for it from travelers who have been in Guyana.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Guyana?
faq.answer: It depends on your passport. CARICOM nationals travel freely and are normally admitted for six months. Citizens of the United States, Canada, the United Kingdom, EU and EEA countries, and a long list of other Commonwealth and Latin American states enter visa-free for up to 90 days for tourism. Everyone else needs a visitor's visa arranged before travel through a Guyanese embassy or high commission.

faq.question: How does CARICOM free movement work in Guyana?
faq.answer: Guyana is a founding member of the Caribbean Community, and nationals of other CARICOM member states are entitled to an automatic stay of six months on arrival under the Revised Treaty of Chaguaramas. Skilled nationals with a CARICOM Skills Certificate can also live and work in Guyana. Bring proof of nationality — a passport is simplest, and is needed for onward flights.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Guyana?
faq.answer: Only if you are arriving from, or have spent more than 12 hours transiting, a country with risk of yellow fever transmission — then a certificate is required from age 1. Guyana itself is a risk country, so vaccination is recommended for everyone, and you will be asked for the certificate when traveling on to Brazil or Suriname.

faq.question: Can I get a visa on arrival in Guyana?
faq.answer: Only as an exception. Travelers from countries with no Guyanese diplomatic representation can be authorized to collect a visa at the port of entry, but this needs written approval from the Ministry of Home Affairs arranged well in advance. Turning up without it risks being refused boarding, so treat the visitor's visa from a Guyanese mission as the normal route.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Guyana?
faq.answer: Yes. Apply at the Central Immigration and Passport Office in Georgetown before the days written in your passport run out. Extensions are usually granted in blocks of up to 90 days for a small fee, and you will need your accommodation details and onward ticket.

faq.question: Is Guyana safe for tourists?
faq.answer: Guyana rewards care rather than nerve. Violent and armed robbery is a real risk in parts of Georgetown, so avoid walking after dark, use booked taxis, and keep valuables out of sight. The interior — Kaieteur, Iwokrama, the Rupununi — is very safe from crime but genuinely remote, with limited medical help, so travel with an established operator and insurance that covers evacuation.
